clue.text: Trump, perhaps, to slip up badly

definitions.note: Donald Trump is an example of a politician appealing directly to ordinary people

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the phrase are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician prone to gaffes and verbal stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles the letters of TO SLIP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump is commonly cited as an example of a politician who courts the masses against the elite.

clue.text: Film course for one with a problem

parts.note: Psycho is the Hitchcock thriller
a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: A film studies module designed for a student who is struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberately understated description of someone with a serious mental disorder.

clue.text: Goodbye to the outside, going in to die in alley

indicators.note: the two outer letters are put into the phrase for dying

parts.note: to pass away is to die

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of the word Goodbye are used

explanation.surface: A farewell outdoors before someone goes into an alley to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outside' takes GE, the ends of Goodbye, and 'going in to' places them inside PASS AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow passage between buildings, a synonym.

clue.text: Waiting period as posh car collects bachelor

indicators.note: the car picks up a passenger, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: A wait while a chauffeured car picks up an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' puts B inside LIMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of uncertain waiting, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: One's group of rebels relaxed at first in comfort

indicators.note: the word for relaxed is placed at the start of the build

parts.note: sat, as in sat back, means relaxed
one's is read as one is, I + S giving IS
a faction is a dissident group within a party

explanation.surface: Someone's rebel band was at ease before finding comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' becomes IS (one is); 'at first' puts SAT ahead of IS and FACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction can mean contentment or consolation, so it matches comfort as a near synonym.

clue.text: Exerts heavy pressure on joint — shortly notices

indicators.note: said briefly, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: A warning about strain on a joint, given in brief notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims KNEE to KNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead dough or muscle is to work it by pressing hard repeatedly.

clue.text: Sounds of foxtrot that are heard in the wings

definitions.text: that are heard in the wings

parts.note: noises are sounds
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The music of a ballroom dance drifting in from offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: Noises Off is a stage direction for sounds made offstage, and the title of a Michael Frayn farce.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction for effects produced offstage, which the audience hears from the wings of a theatre.

clue.text: Family member is cow (not daughter)

indicators.note: not means the letter for daughter is left out

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or daunt them

explanation.surface: A rude remark calling a relative a cow, with the daughter excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is the verb, to intimidate, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a relative, a parent's sister, so an example of a family member.

clue.text: Suggesting Louis XIV collapsed?

indicators.note: only a hint of the title is given, the royal word cut down to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: Louis XIV of France was known as the Sun King

explanation.surface: Asking whether the French monarch fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis XIV was the Sun King; K is the standard abbreviation for king, so 'Suggesting' him gives SUN K.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has sunk has fallen in or caved in, a synonym of collapsed.

clue.text: House in miniature around back of Hyde Park

indicators.note: the house is placed in the middle of the other word
the word for miniature is turned around to run backwards

parts.note: a toy dog or toy poodle is a miniature breed
a semi is a semi-detached house

indicators.note: only the final letter of Hyde is used

explanation.surface: A tiny model house set up at the far end of a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts a model house in a London park, but Hyde only gives its last letter; 'around' turns the miniature word backwards and 'in' sets the house inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California, an example of a park.

clue.text: Haddock, part of it with bread

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish, the it referring to the haddock
naan or nan is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A haddock dish, part of it served with bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the haddock, so part of it is a fin.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnan haddie is smoked haddock from Scotland, so the word names that fish.

clue.text: Fussy car rental

parts.note: a hardtop is a car with a rigid roof
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A customer being particular about a car hire.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fussy is difficult to satisfy, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: King's ambassador fine, say, following commotion

indicators.note: the fine and the saying come after the commotion

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
ado means fuss or commotion
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A monarch's envoy is fined, apparently, after some disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is an example of a nation's chief figurehead.

clue.text: Get people back into perpetual strife? Nothing in it

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the jumbled letters
strife is conflict and disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A question about returning to endless conflict, with nothing to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strife' scrambles PERPETUAL, and 'in it' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To repopulate a town is to resettle it with inhabitants again.

clue.text: From barn, as horse led out, they steer

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H, and led is taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse being led out of a barn by riders guiding it.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is H, slang for heroin, which joins BARN AS LED in the mix that 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Handlebars are how a cyclist controls a bike's direction.

clue.text: Gun, one produced on stage …

definitions.meaning: a dramatic work or play put on in a theatre

explanation.surface: A firearm brought out as a stage prop, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 17 across but has no role in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a firearm and also a word for a play or other stage work.

clue.text: Judge's last case bringing back memories

indicators.note: only the final letter of the judge is used

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case used for addressing someone

explanation.surface: A judge's final trial stirs nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammar, not a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up recollections or feelings of the past.

clue.text: … an animal with no lines stars

indicators.note: the railway lines are removed

parts.note: a dromedary is a one-humped camel
RY, railway, gives lines

explanation.surface: Continuing from 15 across: a creature with no lines becomes a star turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' is RY, railway lines; 'with no' removes it from DROMEDARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation and galaxy, a group of stars.

clue.text: A number shared meal

definitions.meaning: a song, the famous standard from No, No, Nanette
an afternoon snack laid out for a couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'number' means a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a well-known song, and also a description of an afternoon refreshment for a pair of people.

clue.text: Foolish to eat a bit of radicchio leaf

indicators.note: the word for foolish swallows the letter

parts.note: fond in its old sense means foolish

indicators.note: just the opening letter of radicchio

explanation.surface: A daft urge to munch some salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Fond's archaic sense is foolish; 'to eat' puts R inside FOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A frond is the leaf of a fern or palm.

clue.text: Play, with this?

parts.note: Ibsen's drama is a play, and the toy itself is something a child plays with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is the noun, a drama by Ibsen, and the verb, what a child does with the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibsen drama, and a miniature home that children play with.

clue.text: Almost home, where this is?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the hearth is the fireside and so stands for home

explanation.surface: A nod to the saying that home is where this is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home is where the heart is' is the proverb the clue invokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says home is wherever one's affections lie, so the organ of love is the thing found there.

clue.text: Succeeded with hat, lost it with feet?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds with a hat, then loses it at the feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost it with feet' means lost one's footing, as on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who slid lost their footing, an idiomatic and playful paraphrase.

clue.text: Man's house and college spoken of

indicators.note: the name of the college is said out loud

parts.note: Gonville and Caius is a Cambridge college whose name is pronounced ...

explanation.surface: A person's home and university, both mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose parliament's lower chamber is the House of Keys; Caius College, Cambridge, is said 'keys'.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Keys is the elected chamber of the Isle of Man's parliament.

clue.text: Chemist's position serious

parts.note: a lie, as in the lie of the land, is a position
big, as in a big problem, means serious

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's stance is described as grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Justus von Liebig was a 19th-century German chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a German scientist who founded organic chemistry teaching.

clue.text: Forty-eight hours backchat that's boring?

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: forty-eight hours is a day and a day, two days

explanation.surface: Two days of cheeky retorts that turn out to be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A DAY A DAY around; 'backchat' looks like one word but splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to dismiss tedious, repetitive talk, an idiom for blah blah.

clue.text: Representative comes out of bin cleaner

indicators.note: the representative leaves the bin, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a dumpster is a large rubbish skip
MP, Member of Parliament, is a representative

explanation.surface: A politician climbs out of a rubbish bin, perhaps the cleaner for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for cleaning furniture.

clue.text: Relax, supplying energy for one in grief

indicators.note: supplying one thing for another means a swap of letters

parts.note: distress is grief or anguish
I, the Roman numeral, is one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Advice to unwind by putting effort into a sorrowful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplying ... for' swaps I for E in DISTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To de-stress is to unwind and lose tension, a synonym of relax.
